q: Which battery works with the SAJ H2-10K-T3?
a: The batteries below all carry a documented pairing with the H2-10K-T3. Every pair is released with the matching accessory: each battery is operated together with its own control module from the same series. Keep the smallest set in mind — a single module stays below the battery voltage window of this inverter, so the larger sets are the documented choice. q: What is the usable capacity of the Pylontech L260 Omni?

The unit is a liquid-cooled commercial all-in-one system with its PCS integrated, so nominal and usable energy refer to the whole cabinet rather than a separate battery block. The datasheet and the portfolio excerpt are linked on the product card — if you need the usable figure fixed in kWh for a project calculation, tell me the application and I will point you to the right document. ⏎ [cards [2003]]

q: Compare the SAJ H2-10K-T3 and the GoodWe ESA 10 kW.
a: Both units are three-phase home inverters with the same rated AC power (10) and the same maximum PV input (20), so the difference lies in the system concept. The SAJ H2-10K-T3 is a hybrid inverter that you pair with a compatible high-voltage battery, while the GoodWe ESA GW10K-ETA-G20 is the power module of the ESA all-in-one system, where storage is added as modules and the usable capacity spans 5–108 depending on how many you stack. If you plan a larger or later-expandable storage bank, the ESA module concept is the more flexible path; if you already have a battery you want to keep, the SAJ hybrid is the classic route and I can check its documented pairings for you. The comparison below lists the documented specifications side by side. ⏎ [compare {"product_ids": [4107, 3556]}]
